title: Numerous bow shocks in the outer Helix Nebula
comment: Published in Nature, 12 August 2026 issue
summary: Near the end of their lives, low- and intermediate-mass stars expel metal-enriched material in winds and outflows, ultimately producing planetary nebulae (PNe). The ejected material is expected to fragment and mix into the interstellar medium (ISM), but this final assimilation step has been difficult to observe directly. Here we report evidence for this process in the form of twenty-two bow shocks in the eastern outskirts of the Helix Nebula, detected in H$α$ emission with the partially completed MOTHRA telescope. Unlike the large-scale wind-ISM bow shocks commonly observed around evolved stars, the shocks are compact and associated with individual clumps of gas. Going outward from the central star, the radius of curvature $R_c$ decreases by a factor of ~100 over the radial range r=0.4-1.4 pc. This is accompanied by a morphological transition from thin, well-defined bows to fuzzy, patchy structures. We interpret these changes as progressive stripping and fragmentation of AGB-shell remnants as they interact with the ISM. The slope of the observed $R_c - r$ relation implies a loss of fragment coherence on a timescale of ~10,000 yr, providing a rare direct constraint on the time-scale for disruption and entrainment of fragmented stellar ejecta into the ISM.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the first direct evidence of stellar ejecta fragmentation and mixing into the ISM, observed as 22 compact bow shocks in the eastern outskirts of the Helix Nebula detected in Hα emission with the MOTHRA telescope. The bow shocks show a ~100x decrease in radius of curvature over 0.4–1.4 pc, transitioning from thin bows to fuzzy structures, implying fragmentation of AGB-shell remnants on a ~10,000 yr timescale.
AI.motivation: While the ejection of metal-enriched material from low- and intermediate-mass stars into planetary nebulae is well understood, the final step—fragmentation and mixing of the ejected material into the interstellar medium—has been difficult to observe directly. This paper aims to provide direct observational evidence for this process.
AI.method: Observations of the Helix Nebula's eastern outskirts were made in Hα emission using the partially completed MOTHRA telescope. The authors detected 22 compact bow shocks associated with individual clumps of gas, measuring their radius of curvature Rc as a function of radial distance r from the central star (0.4–1.4 pc), and analyzed the morphological transition from thin, well-defined bows to fuzzy, patchy structures.
AI.result: The bow shocks are compact and associated with individual gas clumps. Going outward from the central star, Rc decreases by a factor of ~100 over r=0.4-1.4 pc, accompanied by a morphological transition from thin bows to fuzzy, patchy structures. The slope of the Rc–r relation implies a loss of fragment coherence on a timescale of ~10,000 yr.
AI.conclusion: The observed bow shocks provide rare direct evidence for the stripping and fragmentation of AGB-shell remnants as they interact with the ISM, and yield a direct constraint on the ~10,000 yr timescale for disruption and entrainment of fragmented stellar ejecta into the ISM.

title: From blue to red spirals: Slow galaxy transformation via ram pressure stripping in TNG-50
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Late-type galaxies lose gas through ram-pressure stripping (RPS) after falling into a massive halo. Because this mechanism primarily removes the gaseous component while leaving the stellar disk largely undisturbed, it provides a pathway for quenching star formation without immediate morphological transformation. While RPS is well established in galaxy clusters, galaxy evolution in low-mass groups is often attributed to mergers, leaving open the question of whether RPS alone can drive the transition from blue, star-forming spirals to quenched systems in these environments. We use the high-resolution cosmological simulation TNG-50 to investigate the evolution of blue spiral galaxies, after their infall into group-scale halos. We excluded systems undergoing significant mergers, thus isolating the effect of RPS. We find that RPS in low-mass groups (M$_{group}<10^{14.5}$ M$_{\odot}$) can efficiently quench star formation while preserving the stellar disk structure. The transformation is gradual, with quenching timescales $\gtrsim6$ Gyr after infall, longer than the $\sim4$ Gyr typically associated with merger-driven evolution. The resulting galaxies are predominantly red, anemic spirals rather than fully transformed S0 systems, indicating that gas removal alone is insufficient to produce complete morphological transformation. Our results show that RPS in group environments can generate long-lived quenched spirals which might represent an intermediate evolutionary pathway preceding the formation of lenticular galaxies.

AI.tldr: Using the TNG-50 cosmological simulation, this paper shows that ram-pressure stripping alone (excluding mergers) can efficiently quench star formation in blue spiral galaxies after infall into low-mass group halos (M<10^14.5 M_sun), producing red, anemic spiral galaxies on timescales of ≥6 Gyr—longer than merger-driven quenching (~4 Gyr)—and suggests these quenched spirals represent an intermediate evolutionary step preceding lenticular galaxy formation.
AI.motivation: While ram-pressure stripping is well established in galaxy clusters, it is unclear whether RPS alone can drive the blue-to-quenched transition of spiral galaxies in low-mass group environments, where galaxy evolution is typically attributed to mergers.
AI.method: The authors use the high-resolution cosmological simulation TNG-50 to track blue spiral galaxies after infall into group-scale halos (M<10^14.5 M_sun), excluding systems undergoing significant mergers to isolate the effect of ram-pressure stripping.
AI.result: RPS in low-mass groups can efficiently quench star formation while preserving the stellar disk structure. The transformation is gradual with quenching timescales ≥6 Gyr after infall (longer than the ~4 Gyr associated with mergers). The resulting galaxies are predominantly red, anemic spirals rather than fully transformed S0 systems.
AI.conclusion: Gas removal alone is insufficient for complete morphological transformation; RPS in group environments can generate long-lived quenched spirals, which may represent an intermediate evolutionary pathway preceding the formation of lenticular galaxies.

title: A Helium-shell Burning Blue Horizontal Branch Star Produced from Common Envelope Evolution
summary: Observationally, blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars are defined as hot stars occupying a characteristic region between the extreme blue horizontal branch and RR Lyrae variables in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram. Most of them are interpreted as stripped core-helium-burning stars, but the role of binary interaction in their formation remains unclear. Here, we report the discovery of a metal-rich BHB star in a 0.82628-day binary system (\Feige 64) comprising a $0.35\pm0.03\,M_{\odot}$ BHB star and a likely $1.26\pm0.17\,M_{\odot}$ white dwarf (WD). The BHB star has an effective temperature of $15{,}524\pm310$\, K and a luminosity of $39.7\pm4.1\,L_{\odot}$. Stellar evolution modelling indicates that it is a helium-shell-burning star produced through the common-envelope channel, retaining a hydrogen-rich envelope that is more massive than previously thought for low-mass stars. This finding provides direct evidence for binary interaction in the formation of BHB stars, offering a fresh perspective on interpreting this emerging population.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the discovery of a metal-rich blue horizontal branch (BHB) star in a 0.826-day binary system (Feige 64), consisting of a 0.35 M☉ BHB star and a likely 1.26 M☉ white dwarf. Stellar evolution modeling indicates the BHB star is a helium-shell-burning star formed via the common-envelope channel, providing direct observational evidence for binary interaction in the formation of BHB stars.
AI.motivation: While most BHB stars are interpreted as stripped core-helium-burning stars, the role of binary interaction in their formation has remained unclear. This study aims to determine whether binary evolution, specifically the common-envelope channel, can produce BHB stars.
AI.method: The researchers identified and characterized the BHB star in the Feige 64 binary system through observations, measuring an effective temperature of 15,524 K and luminosity of 39.7 L☉. They then performed stellar evolution modeling to investigate the formation pathway of this BHB star, including its binary configuration and the mass of its hydrogen-rich envelope.
AI.result: The system consists of a 0.35±0.03 M☉ BHB star and a likely 1.26±0.17 M☉ white dwarf in a 0.82628-day orbit. Stellar evolution modeling shows the BHB star is a helium-shell-burning star formed through the common-envelope channel, retaining a hydrogen-rich envelope more massive than previously thought possible for low-mass stars.
AI.conclusion: This finding provides direct evidence that binary interaction plays a key role in the formation of BHB stars, offering a new perspective on this emerging stellar population and challenging previous assumptions about envelope retention in low-mass evolved stars.

title: Magnetic fields in extreme primordial halos: turbulent collapse and implications for early quasar formation
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: It is sometimes suggested that the most massive quasars at high redshift may have formed from rare high-sigma peaks in the cosmic density field. We explore here the evolution in a massive primordial halo corresponding to one of these rare sigma peaks, employing cosmological high-resolution magneto-hydrodynamical zoom-in simulations with initial field strength of $10^{-14}-10^{-8}$ G. The dark matter halo forms at the intersection of strongly convergent flows, leading to the formation of highly supersonic turbulence already on intergalactic scales, with turbulent Mach numbers of order $10-20$ also within the halo. Turbulent magnetic field amplification has never been explored in this regime and we therefore investigate whether this gives rise to effects similar to those observed in more typical halos. While the weaker initial field is somewhat more strongly amplified as a result of the shear flows, overall the evolution in the different simulations is rather similar and the flows are dominated by supersonic turbulence. We show in particular that the turbulent Jeans mass always dominates over the thermal and magnetic Jeans masses, and only on scales of $10^{-2}-10$ pc, the magnetic Jeans mass may become comparable to the thermal one. Our simulations thus strongly suggest the evolution to be dominated by the large-scale dynamics. As established in previous work, we thus expect the formation of central massive objects of a few times $10^4$ M$_\odot$ also in the presence of magnetic fields. The situation is somewhat different from more typical atomic cooling halos, where previous results have indicated a larger relevance of the magnetic Jeans mass on intermediate scales, potentially enhancing the mass of the massive object.

AI.tldr: This paper uses cosmological magneto-hydrodynamical zoom-in simulations to study the evolution of a massive primordial halo formed from a rare high-sigma peak, finding that supersonic turbulence (Mach ~10-20) dominates the evolution. The turbulent Jeans mass always exceeds thermal and magnetic Jeans masses, with the magnetic Jeans mass only comparable to thermal on scales of 10^-2 to 10 pc. Evolution is governed by large-scale dynamics, leading to central massive objects of a few ×10^4 M☉ regardless of magnetic fields, differing from typical atomic cooling halos.
AI.motivation: Massive high-redshift quasars may form from rare high-sigma density peaks, and the evolution in such extreme primordial halos with magnetic fields has not been explored—particularly the regime of turbulent magnetic field amplification under highly supersonic turbulence (Mach numbers 10-20).
AI.method: Cosmological high-resolution magneto-hydrodynamical zoom-in simulations of a massive primordial halo corresponding to a rare high-sigma peak, with initial magnetic field strengths varying from 10^-14 to 10^-8 G.
AI.result: The halo forms at the intersection of strongly convergent flows, generating highly supersonic turbulence (Mach ~10-20). Weaker initial fields are somewhat more amplified by shear flows, but overall evolution is similar across simulations. The turbulent Jeans mass always dominates over thermal and magnetic Jeans masses; only on scales of 10^-2 to 10 pc does the magnetic Jeans mass become comparable to the thermal one.
AI.conclusion: The evolution is dominated by large-scale dynamics, and central massive objects of a few times 10^4 M☉ are expected to form even in the presence of magnetic fields. This differs from typical atomic cooling halos where the magnetic Jeans mass is more relevant on intermediate scales and may enhance the massive object's mass.

title: Disco in the Dust: Reflected light at the bow shock around Betelgeuse's companion explains its observed luminosity
comment: 4 figures, 1 table, submitting to AAS Journals. Comments welcome!
summary: Recent detections of $α$ Orionis B, the putative companion to Betelgeuse, have been reported using multiple instruments and techniques. These include, most recently, a $>6σ$ detection using VLT/SPHERE reported by Montarges+2026. The authors infer a bright companion ($\sim10^{-3}\times$ Betelgeuse's luminosity) with a mass of $2-3\,M_\odot$ and $T_\text{eff}\approx10-12{,}000$\,K, loosely consistent with the uppermost bounds of Howell+2025's recent mass estimate from speckle-imaging. However, it is in tension by a factor of two with the reported mass-exclusion limits via non-detection from a recent HST far-UV campaign (Goldberg+2025). While mass identification from isochrone-fitting (conducted in all cases) is prone to uncertainty, the restrictive HST upper limit on FUV flux precludes the hot, blue emission of a $\gtrsim2\,M_\odot$ main-sequence star. This discrepancy is reconciled by the following hypothesis: these detections observe the reflection of Betelgeuse's own luminosity scattered off the companion's bow shock and wake as it traverses the dusty circumstellar medium. To evaluate the feasibility of this scenario, we draw from custom, filter-specific stellar models computed with MESA, as well as Athena++ simulations of the companion's bow shock in idealized conditions. Importantly, the expansive bow shock from a stellar-mass object necessarily subtends a sizable portion of Betelgeuse's outgoing flux. We find that optical luminosity ratios of $\sim10^{-3}-10^{-4}$ are straightforward to resolve within reasonable assumptions about the companion mass and circumstellar dust, and disfavor a hot $3\,M_\odot$ companion. We thereby reconcile competing mass hypotheses across observational campaigns through proper attribution of the observed brightness, motivating future multi-wavelength campaigns to further characterize this enigmatic system.

AI.tldr: This paper reconciles conflicting mass estimates for α Orionis B, Betelgeuse's putative companion, by proposing that the detected brightness arises from reflected/scattered light off the companion's bow shock and wake in the dusty circumstellar medium, rather than intrinsic emission from a hot main-sequence companion.
AI.motivation: Recent detections of α Orionis B using various instruments (most notably a >6σ detection from VLT/SPHERE by Montarges+2026) infer a 2-3 M⊙ companion, in tension with HST far-UV non-detection limits (Goldberg+2025) that preclude a hot, blue >2 M⊙ main-sequence star. The discrepancy between mass estimates must be resolved.
AI.method: The authors use custom, filter-specific stellar models computed with MESA, along with Athena++ simulations of the companion's bow shock in idealized conditions, to evaluate the feasibility of the reflection scenario. They calculate optical luminosity ratios expected from Betelgeuse's flux being scattered off the companion's bow shock and wake.
AI.result: The expansive bow shock from a stellar-mass object subtends a sizable portion of Betelgeuse's outgoing flux, and optical luminosity ratios of ~10^-3 to 10^-4 are straightforwardly reproduced under reasonable assumptions about companion mass and circumstellar dust. The results disfavor a hot 3 M⊙ companion.
AI.conclusion: The authors reconcile competing mass hypotheses across observational campaigns by attributing the observed brightness to scattered light from the bow shock and wake rather than intrinsic companion emission. This motivates future multi-wavelength campaigns to further characterize the α Orionis B system.

title: Chemistry here and there: Comparison between the CMZ of the Milky Way and NGC 253
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, Proceedings of IAU Symposium 405
summary: For decades, chemical studies in external galaxies have been limited by sensitivity, resolution, bandwidth or a combination of them. A decade of ALMA operations, made the detailed study of the molecular abundances in nearby galaxies a routine job. We can finally bridge the ISM chemistry from Galactic to extragalactic environments, through one to one comparison, albeit probing significantly different scales. The ALMA large program ALCHEMI imaged the chemistry of the starburst galaxy NGC 253 at an unprecedented combination of sensitivity and resolution, achieving a detailed spatially resolved chemical inventory. ALCHEMI probed molecular differences among regions within its CMZ, and allowed the comparison with Galactic environments ranging from hot cores, quiescent molecular clouds and comets. This comparison can be put in the context of available data towards other extragalactic environments. Globally, the comparisons presented here show an astoundingly good correlation between the chemistry in Galactic GMCs and the central molecular zone of NGC 253, ranging scales from 1 pc up to ~0.5 kpc. The wideband sensitivity upgrade of ALMA will expand similar comparisons towards a wider range of Galactic and extragalactic objects.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses how ALMA, particularly through the ALCHEMI large program, has enabled detailed spatially resolved chemical studies of the starburst galaxy NGC 253, revealing remarkably good correlations between Galactic molecular cloud chemistry and extragalactic central molecular zone chemistry across scales from 1 pc to ~0.5 kpc.
AI.motivation: Chemical studies of external galaxies have historically been limited by sensitivity, resolution, and bandwidth. The ALMA wideband sensitivity upgrade, combined with large programs like ALCHEMI, finally allows bridging interstellar medium chemistry from Galactic to extragalactic environments through one-to-one comparisons.
AI.method: The ALCHEMI ALMA large program imaged the chemistry of the starburst galaxy NGC 253 with unprecedented sensitivity and resolution, producing a detailed spatially resolved chemical inventory. Molecular abundances were compared across regions within NGC 253's central molecular zone (CMZ) and against Galactic environments including hot cores, quiescent molecular clouds, and comets, as well as other extragalactic environments.
AI.result: The comparisons show an astoundingly good correlation between the chemistry in Galactic giant molecular clouds (GMCs) and the central molecular zone of NGC 253, spanning scales from 1 pc up to ~0.5 kpc.
AI.conclusion: The wideband sensitivity upgrade of ALMA will enable similar detailed chemical comparisons toward a wider range of Galactic and extragalactic objects, further bridging the discipline of astrochemistry across distance scales.

title: Statistics of Solar Filament Mass based on CHASE Sun-as-a-star Spectroscopic Observations
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters
summary: Filaments are cool and dense plasmas suspended in the hot corona of the Sun and other stars. Accurately estimating their masses is of great significance for understanding subsequent eruptions and induced space weather effects, but it remains hindered by their intrinsic geometric uncertainties, particularly in spatially unresolved stellar observations. To test and calibrate the methods for estimating the masses of stellar filaments, we conduct a statistical Sun-as-a-star analysis of solar filaments, utilizing full-disk H$α$ spectroscopic observations from the Chinese H$α$ Solar Explorer (CHASE). A total of 1346 filaments, covering a period from January 2024 to October 2025, are identified via a machine-learning segmentation model. We construct their virtual sun-as-a-star spectra by spatially integrating the filament regions and then obtain their optical parameters by cloud-model fitting. Upon correcting projection effects, we establish a representative three-dimensional morphological scaling of length, apparent width, and line-of-sight depth ($L:W_{\rm app}:D_{\rm LOS} \approx 4.5:1:1.7$), with a median filament depth of about 8000 km. Interestingly, the Sun-as-a-star estimated mass shows high consistency with the resolved intrinsic mass across the full sample, with a log-space regression slope of 1.07. As the first large-sample Sun-as-a-star study of solar filaments, our results provide empirical constraints on filament geometries and masses, offering a critical reference for estimating stellar filament masses based on H$α$ spectroscopy.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts the first large-sample Sun-as-a-star statistical analysis of solar filaments using CHASE full-disk Hα spectroscopic observations, analyzing 1346 filaments detected via machine learning. Through cloud-model fitting and projection correction, they establish a representative 3D morphological scaling (L:W:D ≈ 4.5:1:1.7), find a median filament depth of ~8000 km, and demonstrate that Sun-as-a-star mass estimates are highly consistent with resolved intrinsic masses (log-space regression slope of 1.07), providing empirical constraints for estimating stellar filament masses.
AI.motivation: Accurate estimation of filament masses is critical for understanding solar/stellar eruptions and space weather effects, but is hindered by geometric uncertainties especially in spatially unresolved stellar observations. This study aims to test and calibrate mass estimation methods for stellar filaments through Sun-as-a-star analysis.
AI.method: Using full-disk Hα spectroscopic data from CHASE (Jan 2024–Oct 2025), 1346 filaments are identified via a machine-learning segmentation model. Virtual sun-as-a-star spectra are constructed by spatial integration of filament regions, then fit with a cloud model to extract optical parameters. Projection effects are corrected to establish a 3D morphological scaling relationship.
AI.result: A representative 3D morphological scaling of L:W_app:D_LOS ≈ 4.5:1:1.7 is established with a median filament depth of ~8000 km. Sun-as-a-star estimated masses show high consistency with resolved intrinsic masses across the full sample, yielding a log-space regression slope of 1.07.
AI.conclusion: As the first large-sample Sun-as-a-star study of solar filaments, the results provide empirical constraints on filament geometries and masses, offering a critical reference for estimating stellar filament masses based on Hα spectroscopy.

title: Testing Covarying Coupling Constants (CCC) against the full SPARC rotation-curve sample: a like-for-like comparison with MOND and NFW
comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 7 tables, a montage of 165 galaxy rotation curves as supplementary material. Comments are welcomed
summary: The Covarying Coupling Constants (CCC) framework, developed to account for high-redshift JWST observations, contains a mechanism -- a covarying-constant effective mass field keyed to local density -- that modifies galactic dynamics without particle dark matter. We test it against the full Spitzer Photometry and Accurate Rotation Curves (SPARC) sample of 175 disc galaxies, extending an earlier study of a few objects. Working in an inverse formulation, in which each model predicts the baryonic rotation curve from the observed one, we compare CCC against Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) and one- and two-parameter Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) haloes on identical footing, using the reduced $χ^2_ν$. We show that the published sharp density turn-off in the earlier study is unphysical and replace it with a smooth transition -- the density-space analogue of the MOND interpolating function, introducing no new parameter. One-parameter smooth-CCC then performs comparably to galaxy-by-galaxy fitted MOND (the lower $χ^2_ν$ in 56 per cent of galaxies, mean $χ^2_ν$ of 2.58 versus 2.65; the paired difference is not significant), while two-parameter NFW shows a substantially broader fit-quality distribution and a larger tail of poor or boundary-limited fits (mean $χ^2_ν\approx 7$). The CCC turn-off density is not universal (scatter 0.82 dex) and correlates with galaxy size, qualitatively consistent with a spherical reconstruction applied to flattened disc systems. Recast as an acceleration, however, $a_t = V_{\rm flat}^2/R_t$ has scatter 0.33 dex (on the 91-galaxy resolved subset) -- matching the MOND scale $a_0$ (0.34 dex) -- and comparable magnitude of order $2 \times 10^{-10}$ m/s$^2$, with its size correlation removed. Though not designed for galactic dynamics, CCC describes rotation curves as well as galaxy-by-galaxy fitted MOND.

AI.tldr: The paper tests the Covarying Coupling Constants (CCC) framework against the full SPARC sample of 175 disc galaxies, comparing it to MOND and NFW halo models. The authors replace an unphysical sharp density turn-off with a smooth transition (the density analogue of MOND's interpolating function) with no new parameters. One-parameter smooth-CCC performs comparably to galaxy-by-galaxy fitted MOND (mean χ²ν of 2.58 vs 2.65, not statistically significant), while two-parameter NFW shows a much broader and worse fit distribution (mean χ²ν ≈ 7). Although not designed for galactic dynamics, CCC describes rotation curves as well as galaxy-by-galaxy fitted MOND.
AI.motivation: To test whether the CCC framework—originally developed to explain high-redshift JWST observations—can account for galactic rotation curves without dark matter, by evaluating it against the full SPARC sample of 175 disc galaxies on identical footing with MOND and NFW halo models.
AI.method: Inverse formulation: each model predicts the baryonic rotation curve from the observed one. CCC is compared to MOND and one-/two-parameter NFW haloes using reduced χ²ν. A physical smooth density transition replaces the earlier sharp density turn-off, paralleling the MOND interpolating function without adding parameters. The CCC turn-off density is examined for universality and correlations with galaxy size, and recast as an acceleration scale.
AI.result: Smooth one-parameter CCC performs comparably to galaxy-by-galaxy fitted MOND (lower χ²ν in 56% of galaxies; mean χ²ν 2.58 vs 2.65; paired difference not significant). Two-parameter NFW shows a substantially broader fit-quality distribution with a larger tail of poor/boundary-limited fits (mean χ²ν ≈ 7). The CCC turn-off density is not universal (0.82 dex scatter) and correlates with galaxy size, but recast as acceleration a_t = V²flat/R_t it has only 0.33 dex scatter on the 91-galaxy resolved subset—matching MOND's a0 (0.34 dex)—with magnitude ~2×10⁻¹⁰ m/s² and its size correlation removed.
AI.conclusion: Despite not being designed for galactic dynamics, the CCC framework describes rotation curves as well as galaxy-by-galaxy fitted MOND, while substantially outperforming two-parameter NFW haloes. The recovered acceleration scale matches MOND's characteristic acceleration a0, suggesting a common underlying scale in galaxy dynamics.

title: Results from the first spectropolarimetric survey of $γ$ Dor pulsators
comment: 26 pages, 11 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary:
Context. Magnetic fields can have an important influence on stellar structure and evolution. In intermediate-mass (A- and F-type) stars, there are many known stars with directly measured strong, globally organized magnetic fields, as well as indications of weak and/or small-scale variable fields. However, among the intermediate-mass $γ$ Dor pulsators, there are no known stars with strong surface magnetic fields.
  Aims. The broad goal of this work is to search for evidence of strong, globally organized fields at the surface of $γ$ Dor pulsators.
  Methods. We identified objects consistent with being $γ$ Dor pulsators based on an analysis of space photometry from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. A spectropolarimetric survey was then conducted on a subset of 47 of these objects, with a precision sufficient to detect dipolar surface magnetic fields down to a threshold of about 10 -- 100 G.
  Results. We detected strong magnetism in three targets. However, upon closer inspection, none of these appear to be genuine $γ$ Dor pulsators. We found no evidence of surface magnetism in any of the remaining 44 objects.
  Conclusions. We conclude that either strong, globally organized magnetic fields and $γ$ Dor pulsation are mutually exclusive, or that such stars are exceedingly rare. A possible explanation is that strong global fields inhibit the excitation mechanism, which prevents $γ$ Dor pulsations from being driven in strongly magnetic intermediate-mass stars. The dipolar surface magnetic field strength upper limits we derive for this sample ($\lesssim$ 50 -- 100 G) provide valuable constraints for surface boundary conditions for asteroseismic models that include magnetism for $γ$ Dor stars.

AI.tldr: A spectropolarimetric survey of 47 candidate γ Dor pulsators detected no genuine strong surface magnetic fields, concluding that strong organized magnetic fields and γ Dor pulsation are either mutually exclusive or exceedingly rare, possibly because magnetism inhibits the pulsation excitation mechanism.
AI.motivation: To search for evidence of strong, globally organized magnetic fields at the surface of γ Dor pulsators, since none have been previously found despite many intermediate-mass A/F-type stars hosting strong magnetic fields.
AI.method: Identified γ Dor pulsator candidates from TESS space photometry, then conducted a spectropolarimetric survey on 47 of these objects with sensitivity to detect dipolar surface fields down to ~10–100 G.
AI.result: Strong magnetism was detected in three targets, but none were genuine γ Dor pulsators upon closer inspection. The remaining 44 objects showed no evidence of surface magnetism, allowing upper limits of ~50–100 G to be set for the sample.
AI.conclusion: Strong globally organized magnetic fields and γ Dor pulsation appear mutually exclusive or exceptionally rare, likely because strong global fields suppress the pulsation excitation mechanism. The field-strength upper limits provide useful constraints for magnetized asteroseismic models of γ Dor stars.

title: Molecule-specific diffusion and desorption of interstellar ices on carbonaceous dust
summary: Interstellar ices form on dust grains in the coldest regions of molecular clouds and preserve key volatile reservoirs that could be incorporated into protoplanetary disks during star and planet formation. However, the effect of the dust surface composition on the ice structure and spectroscopic behavior remains poorly constrained. We present a comparative laboratory study of astrophysically relevant ices (CO, CO2, and H2O) deposited on inert calcium fluoride (CaF2) substrate and carbonaceous dust analogs under interstellar conditions. Infrared spectroscopy and temperature-programmed desorption reveal pronounced molecule-specific infrared spectral responses to the amorphous carbonaceous surface. CO and CO2 both exhibit broadened absorption bands, redshifted band positions, and delayed desorption, arising from thermally activated diffusion into the porous dust matrix and indicating strong molecule-surface interactions. By contrast, H2O varies only very little spectrally and thermally, indicating weak wetting and limited coupling to the substrate. These results provide direct laboratory evidence that dust-ice interfaces can affect the ice structure and desorption kinetics of interstellar ices even in thick ice layers. These findings offer new constraints for interpreting infrared absorption bands in astronomical observations and highlight the importance of surface effects in models of interstellar ice chemistry.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comparative laboratory study showing that the dust surface composition—specifically amorphous carbonaceous grains versus inert CaF2—can significantly alter the spectroscopic and desorption properties of astrophysical ices (CO, CO2, H2O), with CO and CO2 showing strong molecule-surface interactions while H2O remains largely unaffected.
AI.motivation: The effect of dust surface composition on ice structure and spectroscopic behavior of interstellar ices is poorly constrained, yet it is critical for interpreting astronomical observations and modeling ice chemistry during star and planet formation.
AI.method: Comparative laboratory study depositing astrophysically relevant ices (CO, CO2, H2O) on inert CaF2 substrates and amorphous carbonaceous dust analogs under interstellar conditions, using infrared spectroscopy and temperature-programmed desorption.
AI.result: CO and CO2 on carbonaceous surfaces exhibit broadened absorption bands, redshifted band positions, and delayed desorption due to thermally activated diffusion into the porous dust matrix. H2O shows minimal spectral and thermal variation, indicating weak wetting and limited substrate coupling.
AI.conclusion: Dust-ice interfaces can affect ice structure and desorption kinetics of interstellar ices even in thick ice layers, providing new constraints for interpreting infrared absorption bands and highlighting the importance of surface effects in interstellar ice chemistry models.

title: First and Comprehensive Study of V0757 Pup : $γ-$Doradus Pulsator in Detached Eclipsing Binary
comment: 22 pages, 15 figures, submitted to PASJ. Comments are welcome
summary: Pulsating stars in detached eclipsing binary (EA) systems are known for providing many important physical informations which constrain both stellar structure and evolution theories. To date, fewer than 50 $γ$ Doradus (GDOR) stars have been found in eclipsing binary systems, making them important targets to study \textit{g}-mode pulsation inside the stars. We present a comprehensive physical and pulsational analysis of V0757 Pup (TIC 6939791), a detached eclipsing binary system observed by the TESS mission (Sectors 7, 34, 61, and 88) and followed up with ground-based spectroscopy from the Thai National Telescope. By combining light curve modeling with radial velocities derived from medium-resolution spectra, we determined the fundamental stellar and atmospheric parameters with high precision. The system consists of an F2V primary ($M_1=1.305\pm0.026M_\odot, R_1=1.643\pm0.020R_\odot$) and a G1V secondary ($M_2=0.934\pm0.030M_\odot, R_2=0.941\pm0.079R_\odot$). We performed a detailed frequency analysis of the residual light curves, identifying two dominant independent pulsation frequencies at $f\sim0.79$ c/d and $0.98$ c/d. These frequencies, along with the derived pulsation constant ($Q\sim0.6$ d), confirm the primary component as a $γ$ Doradus pulsator. An analysis of Eclipse Timing Variations (ETV) reveals non detection of third body companions with current available dataset, strengthen by the result of \textit{Gaia} astrometric analysis. Evolutionary modeling indicates the system is $\sim2.2$ Gyr old, with the primary expected to fill its Roche lobe in $\sim1$ Gyr. Additionally, we calculate a distance of $d\approx350$ pc based on orbital and SED modeling, which is in excellent agreement with the \textit{Gaia} DR3 parallax distance.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive physical and pulsational analysis of V0757 Pup, a detached eclipsing binary system containing a γ Doradus pulsator, using TESS photometry and ground-based spectroscopy. The system consists of F2V and G1V components with precise physical parameters, and two dominant independent pulsation frequencies (~0.79 and 0.98 c/d) confirm the primary as a γ Doradus star. No third body is detected via ETV or Gaia astrometry, the system age is ~2.2 Gyr, and the derived distance (~350 pc) agrees excellently with Gaia DR3.
AI.motivation: Fewer than 50 γ Doradus stars are known in eclipsing binary systems, yet these systems provide unique and important constraints on stellar structure and evolution theories by combining pulsational properties with fundamental stellar parameters. V0757 Pup presents a valuable opportunity to study g-mode pulsation within the context of a precisely characterized detached eclipsing binary.
AI.method: The authors combine light curve modeling with radial velocities from medium-resolution ground-based spectroscopy (Thai National Telescope) and TESS photometry from four sectors. They perform frequency analysis of residual light curves, derive pulsation constants, analyze Eclipse Timing Variations, incorporate Gaia astrometric data, and use orbital and spectral energy distribution (SED) modeling alongside evolutionary modeling.
AI.result: The system comprises an F2V primary (M1=1.305±0.026 M☉, R1=1.643±0.020 R☉) and a G1V secondary (M2=0.934±0.030 M☉, R2=0.941±0.079 R☉). Two dominant independent pulsation frequencies at 0.79 and 0.98 c/d with Q~0.6 d confirm the primary as a γ Doradus pulsator. No third-body companions were detected via ETV or Gaia astrometry. The system is ~2.2 Gyr old with the primary expected to fill its Roche lobe in ~1 Gyr, and the derived distance of ~350 pc agrees excellently with Gaia DR3 parallax.
AI.conclusion: V0757 Pup is confirmed as a detached eclipsing binary hosting a γ Doradus pulsator in its primary component, providing another rare and well-characterized pulsating star in an eclipsing system. This adds valuable constraints for future studies of stellar structure, evolution, and g-mode pulsation theory.

title: Classifying Quasar Types Without a Spectrum
comment: 22 pages, 15 figures. Accepted for publication in PASP
summary: Distinguishing between Type 1 and Type 2 quasars is important because it helps us understand accretion regimes, black hole mass scaling, disk instabilities and feedback processes in active galaxies. Although spectroscopy provides robust classification, it does not scale well with the millions of quasars observed in modern surveys, as it requires substantial time and resources to acquire a good spectrum. On the photometry side, quasar light curves are always irregularly sampled and affected by the specifics of photometric surveys, making them difficult to analyze. In this work, we show that we can use irregularly sampled light curves from the Zwicky Transient Facility to classify quasar types without a spectrum, using Slepian Wavelet Variance. This technique allows us to decompose the variance of light curves into multiple timescales. We use agglomerative hierarchical clustering to classify 516 Type 1 and 238 Type 2 quasars from the MILLIQUAS catalogue, solely based on their wavelet variance curves. We obtain a recovery rate of 99% for Type 1 and 87% for Type 2 quasars, and the few misclassified quasars show the opposite variability behaviour to their spectral type. In contrast to structure functions and the Damped Random Walk model, Slepian Wavelet Variance offers a complementary, model-independent view of variability across short and long timescales.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that Type 1 and Type 2 quasars can be classified using irregularly sampled light curves from the Zwicky Transient Facility via Slepian Wavelet Variance, achieving 99% recovery for Type 1 and 87% for Type 2 quasars without requiring spectroscopy.
AI.motivation: Distinguishing Type 1 and Type 2 quasars is important for understanding accretion regimes, black hole mass scaling, disk instabilities, and feedback processes. While spectroscopy provides robust classification, it does not scale well with the millions of quasars in modern surveys due to high time and resource requirements. Photometric light curves are challenging because they are irregularly sampled and affected by survey-specific characteristics.
AI.method: The authors apply Slepian Wavelet Variance to decompose the variance of irregularly sampled light curves from the Zwicky Transient Facility into multiple timescales. They then use agglomerative hierarchical clustering to classify 516 Type 1 and 238 Type 2 quasars from the MILLIQUAS catalogue based solely on their wavelet variance curves.
AI.result: The method achieves a recovery rate of 99% for Type 1 and 87% for Type 2 quasars. The few misclassified quasars exhibit variability behavior opposite to their spectral type, suggesting intrinsic variability properties may conflict with spectral classification in those cases.
AI.conclusion: Slepian Wavelet Variance provides a complementary, model-independent view of variability across short and long timescales, offering an effective alternative to structure functions and the Damped Random Walk model for quasar classification without spectroscopy.

title: 1.5D investigation of the Hanle effect in the Ca I 4227 line using partial frequency redistribution. Comparison of synthetic Stokes profiles in Bifrost and MURaM-ChE rMHD models
summary: Modeling scattering polarization in the Ca I 4227 Å line is important for diagnosing chromospheric magnetic fields. We investigate the relative influence of formation heights and magnetic fields, through the Hanle effect, on spatially averaged synthetic Stokes profiles using realistic solar atmospheres. We employ 1D vertical columns from 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the solar chromosphere performed with the Bifrost and MURaM-ChE codes, and solve the 1.5D non-local thermodynamic equilibrium polarized radiative transfer equation including partial frequency redistribution and the Hanle effect. The intensity profiles from both simulations agree at line center, while MURaM-ChE exhibits enhanced wing intensity due to deeper, hotter formation regions. The polarization signals form at greater heights in MURaM-ChE than in Bifrost. In the non-magnetic case, Bifrost produces stronger line-core polarization, whereas MURaM-ChE shows enhanced wing polarization. Including the magnetic fields from the simulations results in stronger Hanle depolarization of <Q>/<I> in Bifrost. The distinct thermal and magnetic structures at the corresponding formation heights therefore produce significantly different polarization profiles. In particular, the Hanle signatures suggest that the line-core formation region in MURaM-ChE is less strongly magnetized than that in Bifrost.

AI.tldr: This study models scattering polarization in the Ca I 4227 Å line using 1D vertical columns from 3D R-MHD simulations (Bifrost and MURaM-ChE) to investigate how formation heights and magnetic fields (via the Hanle effect) affect synthetic Stokes profiles. The two atmospheres yield significantly different polarization profiles due to distinct thermal and magnetic structures at formation heights, with Bifrost showing stronger line-core polarization/depolarization and MURaM-ChE showing enhanced wing polarization and a less magnetized line-core formation region.
AI.motivation: Modeling scattering polarization in the Ca I 4227 Å line is important for diagnosing chromospheric magnetic fields, and understanding how formation heights and magnetic fields influence the observed polarization signals is essential for reliable magnetic field inference.
AI.method: The authors employ 1D vertical columns extracted from 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the solar chromosphere (Bifrost and MURaM-ChE codes) and solve the 1.5D non-local thermodynamic equilibrium polarized radiative transfer equation, including partial frequency redistribution and the Hanle effect.
AI.result: Intensity profiles agree at line center but differ in the wings (MURaM-ChE shows enhanced wing intensity from deeper, hotter regions). Polarization forms at greater heights in MURaM-ChE. In non-magnetic cases, Bifrost produces stronger line-core polarization while MURaM-ChE shows enhanced wing polarization. Including magnetic fields leads to stronger Hanle depolarization of <Q>/<I> in Bifrost, suggesting its line-core formation region is more strongly magnetized than MURaM-ChE's.
AI.conclusion: The distinct thermal and magnetic structures at the respective formation heights in the two atmospheric models produce significantly different polarization profiles, and Hanle signatures indicate the line-core formation region in MURaM-ChE is less strongly magnetized than in Bifrost.

title: Search for a Globular Cluster whose Passage through the Galactic Disk could Trigger the Radcliffe Wave
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to Astrophysical Bulletin
summary: Using a catalog of 152 globular clusters (GCs), their orbits were constructed to determine their intersections with the Galaxy's plane of symmetry. Young open star clusters (OSCs) were selected from the selection zone characteristic of the Radcliffe wave. The Hunt and Reffert catalog served as the source of data on these OSCs. A grouping of 17 OSCs with an average age of 32.7 million years was found. It is compact in coordinate, velocity, and age space. This grouping is shown to be a good candidate for the hypothesis that the Radcliffe wave is generated by the passage of an impactor through the Galaxy's plane of symmetry, with the impactor being the GC NGC~4372. The last time it crossed the galactic plane was 55.5 million years ago, and 22.2 million years later, a burst of star formation occurred at this location, forming a whole group of open-clustered stars, and possibly the Radcliffe wave as a whole.

AI.tldr: Using a catalog of 152 globular clusters, the authors constructed orbits to find their crossings of the Galactic plane. They identified a compact group of 17 young open star clusters (average age 32.7 Myr) in the Radcliffe wave region. They propose that the globular cluster NGC 4372, which last crossed the Galactic plane 55.5 Myr ago, may have triggered a burst of star formation 22.2 Myr later, giving rise to this group of open clusters and possibly the Radcliffe wave itself.
AI.motivation: To test the hypothesis that the Radcliffe wave—a coherent structure of star-forming regions and open clusters—was generated by the passage of an external impactor (specifically a globular cluster) through the Galactic plane of symmetry.
AI.method: Orbits of 152 globular clusters were computed to determine their Galactic-plane intersection points. Young open clusters in the Radcliffe-wave selection zone were taken from the Hunt and Reffert catalog. The spatial, kinematic, and age coherence of these clusters was examined, and their grouping was compared to the predicted crossing time and location of candidate impactor globular clusters.
AI.result: A compact group of 17 open clusters with a mean age of 32.7 Myr was identified. The globular cluster NGC 4372 crossed the Galactic plane 55.5 Myr ago; approximately 22.2 Myr later, a correlated burst of star formation produced this group of open clusters. The spatial-temporal match identifies NGC 4372 as a strong candidate for the impactor responsible for the Radcliffe wave.
AI.conclusion: The findings support the hypothesis that the Radcliffe wave was formed by the passage of the globular cluster NGC 4372 through the Galactic plane, which triggered a burst of star formation and produced the observed grouping of young open clusters.

title: Chemical fingerprints of binary mass transfer in massive stars
comment: Published in Nature Astronomy. Link to the paper: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-026-02943-1
summary: The majority of massive stars are born in close binary systems. As stars expand when they age, mass transfer or even a merger with their companion is inevitable. However, most binary interaction products appear as single stars, such that the main evidence of their exciting past is lost. In a comprehensive grid of detailed massive binary evolution models we find systematic trends in chemical surface abundances that allow identifying the past mass gainers. We develop an analytic framework which is independent of specific evolutionary models, to constrain the amount and composition of the accreted material from their observed surface abundances. This yields tight constraints on the uncertain mass transfer physics in massive binary stars and allows us to reconstruct the past evolutionary history of the progenitor binary system. This method, which is shown to also constrain binary mergers (for example, SN 1987A), is applied to some of the best-studied OB stars so far. For γ Columbae, suggested to be an envelope-stripped star, we show that it is a mass gainer instead, whose companion star likely formed a stripped-envelope supernova. Our results highlight surface abundance measurements as a powerful tool to improve our understanding of massive binary systems evolving towards supernovae and compact object binaries.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an analytic framework using chemical surface abundance measurements to identify past mass gainers in massive binary star systems, constraining the amount and composition of accreted material independent of specific evolutionary models. Applied to γ Columbae and other OB stars, the method also constrains binary mergers like SN 1987A, demonstrating surface abundances as a powerful diagnostic for binary evolution history.
AI.motivation: Most massive stars form in close binaries and undergo mass transfer or mergers, but most interaction products appear as single stars, making their binary past difficult to identify. The authors aim to develop a method to reconstruct the past evolutionary history of binary systems using observable surface abundances, independent of specific evolutionary models.
AI.method: The authors constructed a comprehensive grid of detailed massive binary evolution models to identify systematic trends in chemical surface abundances that mark past mass gainers. They then developed an analytic framework, independent of specific evolutionary models, that uses observed surface abundances to constrain the amount and composition of accreted material. This framework is also shown to constrain binary mergers.
AI.result: The method provides tight constraints on uncertain mass transfer physics in massive binaries. Application to γ Columbae, previously suggested to be an envelope-stripped star, reveals it is actually a mass gainer whose companion likely formed a stripped-envelope supernova. The method also successfully constrains binary mergers, including SN 1987A.
AI.conclusion: Surface abundance measurements are a powerful tool for improving our understanding of massive binary systems evolving toward supernovae and compact object binaries, enabling reconstruction of the past evolutionary history of the progenitor binary system.

title: The effect of galaxy interactions on star formation rates in the COLIBRE simulations
comment: 21 pages, 20 figures; submitted to MNRAS
summary: Observations and theory indicate that galaxy interactions enhance star formation rates (SFRs). However, the degree of enhancement and its dependence on the properties of the interacting galaxies vary across different studies. In this work, we use the COLIBRE simulations of galaxy formation to investigate the effect of interactions on the SFRs of star-forming galaxies at redshift $z\approx0$. The COLIBRE simulations capture the multiphase nature of the interstellar medium and have volumes up to $200^3$ and $400^3$ cMpc$^3$ at m6 (gas and dark-matter particle mass $\sim10^6~\mathrm{M_\odot}$) and m7 ($\sim10^7~\mathrm{M_\odot}$) resolutions, respectively. After constructing samples of interacting galaxies (with mass ratios $>0.1$) and isolated controls, matched in stellar mass, large- and small-scale environment, and redshift, we show that the average specific SFR (sSFR) of interacting galaxies is enhanced by up to a factor of $\approx2$ for separations of $\approx10$ kpc. The enhancement decreases with pair separation but remains significant out to $\approx200$ kpc. The enhancement increases with increasing numerical resolution, is more pronounced in the central regions of galaxies, and decreases with increasing stellar mass at fixed separation. Mergers with higher mass ratios induce stronger sSFR enhancement. We compare our results with observational data from the SDSS, finding good agreement in the dependence of the mean sSFR enhancement on separation, but underpredicting its normalisation by a factor of $\approx2$. Finally, we show that the pre-merger sSFR enhancement of resolved interactions accounts for $\approx2$ per cent of the $z\approx0$ cosmic SFR density.

AI.tldr: Using COLIBRE galaxy formation simulations at z≈0, this study shows that galaxy interactions enhance the specific star formation rate (sSFR) of star-forming galaxies by up to ~2x at separations of ~10 kpc, with the enhancement persisting out to ~200 kpc, varying with resolution, stellar mass, and mass ratio, and accounting for ~2% of the cosmic SFR density.
AI.motivation: While observations and theory indicate that galaxy interactions enhance star formation rates, the degree of enhancement and its dependence on interacting galaxy properties vary across different studies. This work aims to systematically quantify this enhancement using the COLIBRE simulations.
AI.method: The study uses COLIBRE galaxy formation simulations (which capture the multiphase ISM) with volumes up to 200^3 and 400^3 cMpc^3 at m6 (~10^6 M_sun) and m7 (~10^7 M_sun) resolutions. They construct samples of interacting galaxies (mass ratios > 0.1) and isolated controls matched in stellar mass, large- and small-scale environment, and redshift, then measure sSFR enhancement as a function of pair separation.
AI.result: The average sSFR of interacting galaxies is enhanced by up to ~2x at separations of ~10 kpc, declining with separation but remaining significant out to ~200 kpc. The enhancement increases with numerical resolution, is more pronounced in central regions, decreases with stellar mass, and is stronger for higher mass-ratio mergers. Good agreement with SDSS observations in the separation dependence is found, though the normalization is underpredicted by ~2x. Pre-merger enhancements contribute ~2% of the z≈0 cosmic SFR density.
AI.conclusion: Galaxy interactions produce a modest but significant enhancement in sSFR that depends on separation, resolution, stellar mass, and mass ratio. Simulations reproduce the qualitative observational trends from SDSS but underpredict the magnitude, and the cumulative contribution of interactions to the cosmic SFR density at z≈0 is small (~2%).

title: New constraints on the binary system HD 327083 and its gaseous and dusty environments
comment: 15 pages, 19 figures, published in A&A
summary: Binary systems with circumbinary molecular and dust rings are of great interest because they provide insights into the dynamics and evolution of stellar systems and the chemistry of the surrounding material. We aim to elucidate the nature of the B[e] binary system HD 327083 and the physical properties of its circumstellar and circumbinary envelopes. We combined multi-epoch high-spectral resolution optical and near-IR observations with VLTI/MIDI observations and ASAS-3 photometry. The data were analysed to obtain the orbital parameters, study individual members of the system, and derive the properties of the atomic and molecular gas and the dusty components of the complex environment of HD 327083. We improved the orbital solution of HD 327083 and derived a period of P = 107.699 d. Most optical lines display variations in shape and intensity when folded with the orbital motion. We assigned F6 II-III and B1 spectral types respectively to the cool and hot components. A ring of molecular gas revolves around the system and varies with the orbital phase. The MIDI data show a silicate band in absorption at 9.7 micron and indicate that the dust distribution has an elliptical shape, with its inner edge varying with orbital phase between 12.5 and 44 AU. We conclude that the B[e] binary system HD 327083 comprises a B-type massive accreting star, and an F-type companion filling over 60% of its Roche lobe and evolving towards the red supergiant stage. The deformed shape of the F-type star causes a broad minimum in the light curve. The hot companion (26 000 K, log g = 3.0) is hidden by a compact disc and shows a bi-polar outflow. The entire binary system presents an O-rich environment. It is surrounded by warm CO and SiO molecular rings, which are enclosed by an elliptical dust structure. All these components were formed by the evolved donor star during its evolution towards the red supergiant phase.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the B[e] binary system HD 327083 using multi-epoch optical/near-IR spectroscopy, VLTI/MIDI interferometry, and ASAS-3 photometry, determining a 107.7-day orbital period, classifying the stars as F6 II-III and B1, and revealing a complex environment of a molecular CO/SiO ring, an elliptical dust structure, and O-rich circumbinary material formed by the evolving donor star.
AI.motivation: Binary systems with circumbinary molecular and dust rings are of great interest because they provide insights into the dynamics and evolution of stellar systems and the chemistry of the surrounding material. The authors aim to elucidate the nature of the B[e] binary system HD 327083 and the physical properties of its circumstellar and circumbinary envelopes.
AI.method: Combined multi-epoch high-spectral-resolution optical and near-IR observations with VLTI/MIDI observations and ASAS-3 photometry. Data were analyzed to obtain orbital parameters, study individual members, and derive properties of atomic/molecular gas and dusty components.
AI.result: Improved orbital solution with P = 107.699 d; spectral types F6 II-III (cool) and B1 (hot); molecular gas ring varies with orbital phase; MIDI shows silicate absorption at 9.7 micron with elliptical dust distribution whose inner edge varies (12.5-44 AU); system comprises a B-type accreting star and an F-type companion filling over 60% of its Roche lobe.
AI.conclusion: HD 327083 is a B[e] binary with a B-type massive accreting hot star (26,000 K, log g = 3.0) hidden by a compact disc with bi-polar outflow, and an F-type companion evolving toward the red supergiant stage. The system has an O-rich environment surrounded by warm CO and SiO molecular rings enclosed by an elliptical dust structure, all formed by the evolved donor star.

title: The Shape of the Vertical Action Distribution Locates the Scatterers that Heat the Galactic Disc
comment: 30 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to the OJAp
summary: The Milky Way's stellar disc is thicker than the cold gas layer from which its stars form. What scatters stars onto orbits with greater vertical motion remains unresolved. Scatterers could fill the disc volume, as bending waves or dark substructure would, or could be confined to the midplane, as giant molecular clouds are. Scattering from a midplane layer occurs only during the fast plane-crossing phase and becomes less effective as that speed increases, whereas a volume-filling perturbation remains effective near the slow turning points. We derive the distribution of vertical action this leaves behind, for any height distribution of scatterers. The geometry turns out to enter only through the logarithmic slope of the diffusivity in action, $D\propto J_z^{b}$, and solving the Fokker-Planck equation gives $p(J_z)\propto\exp[-(J_z/J_0)^{2-b}]$. Scatterers that fill the volume give $b=1$ and an exponential, a thin layer at the midplane gives $b=1/2$ and a sharper cutoff: the shape of $p(J_z)$ records where the scatterers sit, the growth of its scale how strongly they scatter. We fit this model to 7589 low-$α$ red clump stars of Ting & Rix (2019) between 5 and 10 kpc and 2 and 8 Gyr old, leaving the heating history free. This yields $b=0.51^{+0.06}_{-0.07}$, consistent with the thin-layer prediction but not the volume-filling one. Comparing the 2-4 Gyr heating amplitude with the present molecular surface density gives an effective scatterer mass of $2.7\times10^{6}\,M_\odot$. Older stars have experienced more of the Galaxy's gas-richer past; correcting for that history brings all four age bins to $(1.9-2.8)\times10^{6}\,M_\odot$, inside the range cloud catalogues and mass functions give. The Milky Way's disc is heated near the plane, by an evolving population of objects of giant-molecular-cloud mass.

AI.tldr: The paper derives the distribution of vertical action left behind by scatterers depending on their height distribution in the galactic disc. Scatterers confined to the midplane (like giant molecular clouds) produce a sharper cutoff in the action distribution ($b=1/2$) while volume-filling scatterers (like bending waves or dark substructure) produce an exponential ($b=1$). Fitting to 7589 low-α red clump stars yields $b=0.51^{+0.06}_{-0.07}$, consistent with thin-layer (midplane) scattering. The inferred effective scatterer mass of $2.7\times10^6\,M_\odot$ (corrected to $1.9-2.8\times10^6\,M_\odot$ across age bins after accounting for the gas-richer past) matches cloud catalogues, indicating giant molecular clouds now born near the plane heat the disc.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing puzzle of what scatters stars in the Milky Way's disc onto orbits with greater vertical motion (thicker disc than the cold gas layer). The authors aim to discriminate between volume-filling scatterers (bending waves, dark substructure) and midplane-confined scatterers (giant molecular clouds) by the shape of the vertical action distribution.
AI.method: The authors derive that the distribution of vertical action $p(J_z)$ from Fokker-Planck theory depends only on the logarithmic slope $b$ of the diffusivity $D\propto J_z^b$, giving $p(J_z)\propto\exp[-(J_z/J_0)^{2-b}]$. A volume-filling distribution gives $b=1$ (exponential) while a thin midplane layer gives $b=1/2$ (sharper cutoff). This model is fit to 7589 low-α red clump stars from Ting & Rix (2019) between 5-10 kpc and 2-8 Gyr, with the heating history left free.
AI.result: The fit yields $b=0.51^{+0.06}_{-0.07}$, consistent with the thin-layer prediction but excluding the volume-filling one. Comparing the 2-4 Gyr heating amplitude with the present molecular surface density gives an effective scatterer mass of $2.7\times10^6\,M_\odot$. After correcting for the gas-richer past of older stars, all four age bins converge to $(1.9-2.8)\times10^6\,M_\odot$, within the range given by cloud catalogues and mass functions.
AI.conclusion: The Milky Way's disc is heated near the plane by an evolving population of objects of giant-molecular-cloud mass, establishing giant molecular clouds as the dominant vertical heating mechanism rather than volume-filling perturbations like bending waves or dark substructure.

title: Deep MUSE observations of SNR 0509-67.5 reveal a double degenerate merger progenitor
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, supplementary materials
summary: Deep MUSE observations of SNR 0509-67.5 reveal that the coronal [Fe\,\textsc{xiv}] $\mathrmλ$5303 emission line appears with either one or two velocity components across the entire remnant, arising from reverse-shocked ejecta moving toward and away from the observer. A supervised dense neural network classifies each spaxel and fits Gaussian profiles plus a linear function to the observed line emission. We measure a bulk Doppler velocity of $-1000\pm60~~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$, interpreted as the line-of-sight component of the primary white dwarf's orbital velocity in a double-degenerate merger. The red- and blue-shifted ejecta map shows a flattened edge along the north-eastern rim, consistent with the companion's shadow, indicating a binary companion was present at explosion. Modelling this feature as a cone anchored at the explosion centre and applying Bayesian inference, we recover the cone's orientation and half-opening angle. We then use the Eggleton Roche-lobe relation to infer properties of the companion. The companion was likely a ${\sim}0.6~\mathrm{M_\odot}$ white dwarf with radius ${\sim}9800$~km and orbital velocity ${\sim}1700~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$ at the time of explosion. Together, these results provide a complete dynamical picture of a Type Ia supernova progenitor system whose maximum-light spectrum is independently constrained by light echo observations.

AI.tldr: Using deep MUSE observations of SNR 0509-67.5, the authors analyze the coronal [Fe XIV] λ5303 emission line to reveal a double-degenerate merger scenario for a Type Ia supernova. A neural network classifies spaxels and fits Gaussian profiles, revealing a bulk Doppler velocity of -1000 km/s and a flattened edge along the northeastern rim—interpreted as the companion's shadow. Bayesian cone modeling and the Eggleton Roche-lobe relation recover the cone orientation and infer a ~0.6 M⊙ white dwarf companion with ~9800 km radius and ~1700 km/s orbital velocity at explosion.
AI.motivation: To provide a complete dynamical picture of a Type Ia supernova progenitor system by directly observing and modeling kinematic signatures of the reverse-shocked ejecta and the surviving companion in a double-degenerate merger scenario.
AI.method: MUSE observations of the [Fe XIV] λ5303 line; a supervised dense neural network classifies each spaxel and fits Gaussian profiles plus a linear function; Bayesian inference is applied to model the companion shadow feature as a cone anchored at the explosion centre; the Eggleton Roche-lobe relation is used to infer the companion's physical properties.
AI.result: A bulk Doppler velocity of -1000±60 km/s is measured, interpreted as the line-of-sight component of the primary white dwarf's orbital velocity. Red- and blue-shifted ejecta maps show a flattened northeastern edge consistent with a companion shadow. Modeling recovers the cone's orientation and half-opening angle, yielding a companion of ~0.6 M⊙ white dwarf, radius ~9800 km, and orbital velocity ~1700 km/s at explosion.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a complete dynamical picture of a Type Ia supernova progenitor system in a double-degenerate merger, with a binary companion present at explosion, independently supported by light echo observations constraining the maximum-light spectrum.

title: Evidence for the First Globular Cluster Stellar Stream beyond the Milky Way
comment: 18 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. This version of the article has been accepted for publication in Nature, after peer review, but does not reflect post-acceptance improvements. The Version of Record is available online at: http://dx.doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10878-w
summary: The dark matter content of ultra-diffuse galaxies is the subject of considerable debate. Stellar streams, which form when a host galaxy tidally strips stars from an orbiting stellar system, provide a powerful technique to constrain the dark matter content of external galaxies. The stripped stars form long, thin leading and trailing tidal arms that persist for billions of years. Stellar streams from globular clusters are particularly sensitive probes of dark matter halos and substructure. Globular cluster streams are expected to exist in a variety of host galaxy types, but so far, they have only been observed in the Milky Way. We present evidence for the first extragalactic globular cluster stellar stream, identified in deep Hubble Space Telescope imaging of the ultra-diffuse galaxy, UGC9050-Dw1. The stream's morphology, colour, and apparent association with a compact source support the globular cluster progenitor interpretation observationally, and we reproduce the observed surface brightness with simulated globular cluster stellar populations. We use generative stream modelling, which fits dynamical models directly to the stream morphology, to constrain the mass of the progenitor and present the first stream-based halo constraint for an ultra-diffuse galaxy. The stream models point to a globular cluster origin and suggest a massive dark matter host halo. By extending the reach of globular cluster stream analysis to external galaxies, this work opens a new chapter in dark matter science.

AI.tldr: First detection of an extragalactic globular cluster stellar stream in the ultra-diffuse galaxy UGC9050-Dw1 using deep Hubble Space Telescope imaging, providing the first stream-based dark matter halo constraint for an ultra-diffuse galaxy.
AI.motivation: To resolve the debate over the dark matter content of ultra-diffuse galaxies by using stellar streams—particularly those from globular clusters—as sensitive probes of dark matter halos and substructure. Previously, globular cluster streams had only been observed in the Milky Way.
AI.method: The authors identified the stream using deep Hubble Space Telescope imaging of UGC9050-Dw1. They assessed the stream's morphology, colour, and association with a compact source to support the globular cluster progenitor interpretation, reproduced the observed surface brightness with simulated globular cluster stellar populations, and applied generative stream modelling that fits dynamical models directly to the stream morphology to constrain the progenitor mass and host halo.
AI.result: The stream models indicate a globular cluster origin and suggest a massive dark matter host halo for UGC9050-Dw1. The observed surface brightness was reproduced with simulated globular cluster stellar populations, and the first stream-based halo constraint for an ultra-diffuse galaxy was obtained.
AI.conclusion: This work extends globular cluster stream analysis to external galaxies, opening new avenues for dark matter science and providing a powerful technique to constrain dark matter halos in a broader range of galaxy types.

title: Nascent Embedded-protostar Survey in Taurus (NEST) I: Protostellar Multiplicity
summary: We present new ALMA 0.9 mm and VLA 9 mm observations in the Taurus Molecular Cloud (TMC) of 25 protostellar systems, containing 40 protostars, observed at 0.3" (~20 au) resolution. Within separations of 18-10,000 au, the ALMA/VLA-observed Taurus sample has a multiplicity fraction (MF), defined as the fraction of systems with at least one companion, of 0.50 +/- 0.07, and a companion fraction (CF), defined as the average number of companions per system, of 0.58 +/- 0.20. To build a more complete census of protostellar multiplicity in this region, we supplement the observed sample with 24 protostars (12 protostellar systems and 5 additional companions associated with systems we observed) previously identified through archival infrared or ALMA observations. Together, these 64 individual protostars (37 systems) define our Taurus+ sample, for which we measure higher values of 0.53 +/- 0.06 and 0.72 +/- 0.19 for the MF and CF, respectively. These multiplicity statistics in the TMC are notably higher than those reported in the more clustered star-forming regions of Orion and Perseus at the ~3-4 sigma level, suggesting that Taurus may preserve a larger fraction of primordial multiples. The separation distributions in our samples show populations of both close and wide multiples, but a deficit at intermediate separations of 200-300 au. This pattern may suggest two distinct formation pathways: close binaries (<200 au) arising primarily from disk fragmentation, and wide multiples (>1000 au) from core fragmentation.

AI.tldr: New ALMA/VLA observations of 25 protostellar systems (40 protostars) in Taurus at ~20 au resolution reveal a multiplicity fraction of 0.50 and companion fraction of 0.58, which increase to 0.53 and 0.72 when supplemented with archival data (Taurus+ sample of 37 systems). Taurus multiplicity is significantly higher than Orion and Perseus, and the separation distribution shows a deficit at 200-300 au, suggesting two distinct formation pathways: disk fragmentation for close binaries (<200 au) and core fragmentation for wide multiples (>1000 au).
AI.motivation: To construct a more complete census of protostellar multiplicity in the Taurus Molecular Cloud at high angular resolution, and to compare these statistics with other star-forming regions to constrain the mechanisms of binary and multiple system formation.
AI.method: Observations at 0.3" (~20 au) resolution using ALMA at 0.9 mm and VLA at 9 mm of 25 protostellar systems containing 40 protostars. The sample was supplemented with 24 additional protostars (12 systems and 5 companions) from archival infrared and ALMA observations to form the Taurus+ sample of 64 protostars across 37 systems.
AI.result: The ALMA/VLA-observed sample yields MF = 0.50 +/- 0.07 and CF = 0.58 +/- 0.20; the Taurus+ sample yields MF = 0.53 +/- 0.06 and CF = 0.72 +/- 0.19. These values are higher than those in Orion and Perseus at the 3-4 sigma level. The separation distribution shows a deficit at intermediate separations (200-300 au), with distinct populations of close (<200 au) and wide (>1000 au) multiples.
AI.conclusion: Taurus exhibits notably higher protostellar multiplicity compared to more clustered regions like Orion and Perseus, potentially retaining a larger fraction of primordial multiples. The bimodal separation distribution with a deficit at 200-300 au supports two distinct formation pathways: disk fragmentation producing close binaries and core fragmentation producing wide multiples.

title: A systematic comparison of green valley selection criteria across multiparameter spaces using a homogeneous ultraviolet-optical dataset
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures
summary: We present a systematic comparison of commonly adopted green valley (GV) selection criteria by examining their distributions across multiple observational and physical parameter spaces. Using a homogeneous ultraviolet-optical dataset constructed from the Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX) and the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), we construct GV samples based on rest-frame $u-r$ and NUV$-r$ colours, specific star formation rate, and the $D_n(4000)$ spectral index. These samples are analysed in colour--stellar mass, colour--magnitude, and star formation rate--stellar mass diagrams. We find that the different selection criteria identify statistically distinct subsets of GV galaxies occupying different regions of parameter space. Ultraviolet-based selections are compact in NUV$-r$ colour space but shift toward optically red galaxies and lower star formation activity in the star formation rate--stellar mass plane. The $u-r$-selected sample is more tightly confined in optical colour space but is biased toward higher star formation rates, whereas the $D_n(4000)$-based selection yields the most heterogeneous population. In contrast, the sSFR-selected GV sample exhibits the most consistent behaviour across all parameter spaces. Despite these differences, all selection methods span a similar stellar mass range, indicating that the observed variations arise primarily from differences in star formation activity rather than stellar mass. The relatively small overlap between the different selection criteria demonstrates that GV identification is strongly diagnostic-dependent and that the commonly adopted one-dimensional definitions are not interchangeable. These results highlight the importance of combining complementary diagnostics to obtain a more complete and physically meaningful picture of transitional galaxy populations.

AI.tldr: A systematic comparison of five common green valley (GV) galaxy selection criteria (u-r colour, NUV-r colour, sSFR, D_n(4000)) shows they identify statistically distinct, only partially overlapping galaxy populations, with sSFR selection being most consistent across parameter spaces and all methods spanning similar stellar mass ranges—indicating GV identification is strongly diagnostic-dependent.
AI.motivation: Green valley galaxies represent a transitional population between star-forming and quiescent galaxies, but numerous selection criteria exist in the literature (e.g., rest-frame u-r colour, NUV-r colour, sSFR, D_n(4000)). A systematic comparison of how these criteria differ in the galaxies they select is needed to determine whether these methods are interchangeable and to understand the physical implications of each choice.
AI.method: Using a homogeneous ultraviolet-optical dataset from GALEX and SDSS, the authors construct GV galaxy samples based on four selection criteria: rest-frame u-r colour, NUV-r colour, specific star formation rate (sSFR), and the D_n(4000) spectral index. These samples are then analysed and compared across colour–stellar mass, colour–magnitude, and star formation rate–stellar mass diagrams.
AI.result: The different selection criteria identify statistically distinct subsets of GV galaxies occupying different regions of parameter space. Ultraviolet-based selections are compact in NUV-r colour space but shift toward optically red galaxies and lower star formation activity. The u-r-selected sample is tightly confined in optical colour space but biased toward higher SFRs, while D_n(4000) selects the most heterogeneous population. The sSFR-selected sample shows the most consistent behaviour across all parameter spaces. All methods span a similar stellar mass range, but the overlap between criteria is relatively small.
AI.conclusion: GV identification is strongly diagnostic-dependent and one-dimensional selection criteria are not interchangeable. Since variations arise primarily from differences in star formation activity rather than stellar mass, combining complementary diagnostics is necessary to obtain a more complete and physically meaningful picture of transitional galaxy populations.

title: Hemispheric Asymmetry of Solar Active Regions Arises from a Nested Population
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 1 table
summary: We investigate the longitude--time distribution of NOAA active regions (ARs) during Solar Cycles 22--24 and find statistically significant North--South asymmetry in AR emergence. Using an activity-nest identification algorithm, we show that this asymmetry is concentrated in the subset of ARs that participate in nests. Nest-member ARs exhibit substantially larger hemispheric asymmetry than either the full AR population or the non-nest population, and the asymmetry is largely removed when nest-member ARs are excluded. Monte Carlo tests with randomized longitudes and temporal perturbations show that the observed nesting and asymmetry exceed random expectations, implying that $\sim$6--18\% of ARs participate in a non-random, hemispherically asymmetric nesting component. This asymmetry is associated with temporally offset bursts of activity and distinct longitudinal clustering between the hemispheres, leading to reduced cross-equatorial coherence in the longitude--time distribution of solar ARs.
